title: Science–policy interface

definition.text: The meeting ground where scientists and policy-makers work together so that research can inform, and be guided by, decisions.

facts.text: IPBES was established by governments in 2012 to strengthen the science-policy interface for biodiversity and ecosystem services.
The IPCC was the first of three global science-policy panels, followed by IPBES in 2012 and a panel on chemicals, waste and pollution in 2025.
Translating research into governance is hard because science and politics treat uncertainty very differently.
A review of pollution found a lack of a globally supported formal science–policy interface to inform action, research and funding.

related: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services

definition.text: The rules and agreements that govern how states share transboundary waters, meaning rivers, lakes, seas or groundwater bordered by two or more states.

facts.text: Countries negotiate transboundary water agreements to reduce the risk of conflict, but many shared international rivers still lack treaties.
Such agreements often focus on water infrastructure and water quality.
The UNECE Water Convention on transboundary watercourses and international lakes, signed in Helsinki in 1992, entered into force on 6 October 1996.
Its principles of 'prior appropriation' and 'riparianism' can worsen conflict by legally fixing who has water abundance and who has scarcity.
